Rule: Pick one: wordmark, lettermark, pictorial mark, abstract mark, combination mark, emblem, mascot
Check: Name which type it is and why
Keywords: logo wordmark lettermark pictorial abstract emblem mascot
Notes: A combination mark needs the symbol and the wordmark to work alone too.

Rule: The mark must read at its smallest use
Check: Test at 16 px (screen) and 15 mm wide (print)
Keywords: logo small size favicon minimum legibility
Notes: If it fails, make a simplified small-size version.

Rule: Provide a single-colour version that works on light and on dark
Check: Render it in black and in white on a flat background
Keywords: logo one colour mono black white reversed
Notes: Gradients and effects are not part of the mark.

Rule: Keep a margin around the mark free of other elements
Check: At least a defined unit (for example the height of the symbol's cap) on every side
Notes: Define the unit in the guidelines and show it.

Check: No raster images, no tiny gaps, no strokes thinner than 1/20 of the mark's height
Notes: Outline strokes for the final file.

Rule: Convert text to outlines in the delivered file
Check: No live text element in the final SVG or PDF
Blur it or reduce it to a silhouette: is it still itself?
Notes: Compare against five competitors before keeping it.

Check: No drop shadows, bevels or stock gradients
Notes: Effects belong to applications of the mark, not the mark.

Rule: Provide horizontal, stacked and icon-only lockups
Check: Each has its own minimum size
Notes: Name each variant in the file name.

Rule: Mark and background should differ clearly
Check: Text-sized elements at least 4.5:1; large or graphic parts at least 3:1
Notes: Provide a version for each background in the palette.

Rule: Deliver SVG, PDF (vector) and PNG at 1x and 2x, in colour and one colour
Check: SVG optimised, PNG with a transparent background
Keywords: logo files deliver svg png pdf set

Rule: Define primary and secondary colours with values for screen and print
Check: HEX, RGB, CMYK and a Pantone reference for each
Keywords: brand palette colour hex cmyk pantone
Notes: Print values come from a proof, not a formula, for brand colours.

Rule: One display face, one text face, a fallback for each
Check: Licences cover the use (web, print, app)
Notes: Check the licence before delivering a font to a client.

Rule: Every piece uses the same palette, type scale and mark rules
Check: Compare each new piece with the brand's tokens
Notes: Brand gates belong to the author: propose changes, never write them.
